title: Longest String Chain
statement:
`words` is a list of words made of lowercase English letters. Word `a` is a **predecessor** of word `b` when adding exactly one letter to `a` (at the front, at the end or between two letters, leaving the other letters in their order) produces `b`.

A **chain** is a sequence of one or more words taken from `words` in which every word is a predecessor of the word after it; a single word on its own is a chain of length 1. Return the length of the longest chain that can be formed.
constraints: words[i] contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

This is a longest-increasing-subsequence problem in disguise: a chain only ever moves to a word that is one letter longer, so if words are processed from shortest to longest, every possible predecessor of a word has already been handled. The LIS-style brute force compares every pair of words, O(n² · L). Instead of searching forward, go backwards: a word of length L has at most L predecessors, one for each letter you can delete, and a hash map tells instantly whether that shorter word is in the list and how long its best chain is.

## Approach

1. Copy `words` into `sorted`, ordered by length.
2. `chain` maps each processed word to the length of the longest chain ending at it.
3. For each `word`, start with `length = 1` (the word alone).
4. For every position `i`, delete that letter to get `shorter`; if `shorter` is in `chain`, the word can extend that chain, so `length` may become `chain.get(shorter) + 1`.
5. Store `length` for the word and keep the overall maximum in `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

Sorted by length: `a, b, ba, bca, bda, bdca`.

- `a` and `b`: no shorter words, so each gets 1.
- `ba`: deleting gives `a` (1) and `b` (1), so `ba` gets 2.
- `bca`: deletions `ca`, `ba` (2), `bc`; it gets 3. `bda` likewise gets 3 through `ba`.
- `bdca`: deletions `dca`, `bca` (3), `bda` (3), `bdc`; it gets 4.

`best` ends at 4.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n + n · L²), with L ≤ 16: sorting, then L deletions per word, each building a string of length L.
- Space: O(n · L) for the map and the sorted copy.

## Pitfalls

- Process words in order of length; otherwise a predecessor may be looked up before its own chain length is known.
- A predecessor must keep the other letters in order: `"abc"` does not lead to `"bacd"`.
- Words in the list can repeat; storing the same word twice in the map is harmless.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `sorted` | the words ordered from shortest to longest |
| `chain` | word → length of the longest chain ending at that word |
| `word` | the word being processed |
| `length` | best chain length ending at `word` found so far |
| `i`, `shorter` | the deleted position and the word left after deleting it |
| `best` | the longest chain found overall |
